Police was informed vide GD No. 51A upon which IO alongwith Ct. Vipin reached at spot.
The motorcyclist was found to be shifted to Dr. BSA Hospital vide MLC no. 13709 and was declared brought dead.

After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed by this Tribunal on 29.07.2024: -
1.

Whether deceased Manish Kr Chaudhary, S/o Sh. Vinod Kr Chaudhary expired due to injuries suffered in road traffic accident on 18.10.2023 at around 01:00 P.M., at Pillar No. RHE-6, Under Rohini East Metro Station, Rithala Road, Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing no. DL 51 GD 9659 which was being driven by driver Sanjay, on the said date, time and place?

2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

sentences.text: conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs.
Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also in another case Mangla Ram

14 . The involvement of offending vehicle of the respondent no.2 in accident is not only undisputed but also corroborated by the documentary evidence collected in FIR No. 638/2023 as the vehicle was seized from the spot.
It is claim of R1 that while deceased was trying to overtake the offending vehicle from behind, it came in contact of offending vehicle which resulted into accident.
Footages of CCTV cameras installed in the offending vehicle were also seized by the IO during investigation.

Footage of the rear camera of offending vehicle clearly shows that it was the offending vehicle which changes its lane abruptly due to which the deceased who was on the motorcycle came in contact of rear portion of the bus.

It is claimed MACT Case No. 49/24 (FIR no. 638/23) Seema Choudhary &
Ors. Vs. Sanjay &Ors.

by R1 that it was deceased who tried to overtake the offending vehicle from behind and came in contact of the offending vehicle due to which accident occurred.
But the CCTV footage filed on record do speak contrary to the version of R1.
Therefore, the case does not warrant any other best evidence.

Keeping in view the facts & evidence produced by the petitioner, it is established that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle being driven by respondent No.1.
Record of medical treatment reveals that the cause of death which is consistent with the history of RTA.
Hence, the issue no
. 1 is decided in favour of petitioners.

sentences.text: As per DAR, deceased was about 32 years old on the date of accident.

It is claimed by petitioners that deceased was a Assistant Floor Manager in M/s Safeguard India and was earning Rs. 72,370/-
per month.
Pw1 has proved salary slip of deceased as Ex.Pw1/3 and his bank account statement showing credit of salary Ex.Pw1/4.

However, it is claimed by respondents that the pay slip Ex.Pw1/3 showing the gross salary of deceased i.e. without deduction of tax and it is also not proved on record that if the deceased used file any ITR.
Therefore, there has to be deduction of TDS before fixing the salary of deceased for compensation.
Considering the salary of deceased, it can be fairly assumed that his salary falls under tax and he used to pay Rs. 38,000/- annually as tax from his salary.
Therefore, the income of the deceased, as on the date of the accident i.e. 18.10.223, after deducting TDS (Rs. 3,167 per month) was Rs. 69,203/- per month.

Counsel for the petitioners further argued that future MACT Case No. 49/24 (FIR no.
638/23) Seema Choudhary & Ors. Vs. Sanjay &Ors.

19. Accordingly, on the basis of aforementioned documents, age of the deceased is taken as 32 years as on the date of accident.

Hence, the multiplier of "16" would be applicable in view of pronouncement made in case titled as Sarla Verma (supra).
20.
Claimant/petitioners are mother, father (expired during trial), one sister and one brother.
It is claim of petitioners that petitioner no. 2 Vinod Kumar Chaudhary, father of deceased, was driver but from the year 2020 he was not well and was doing nothing.
It is also claimed that petitioner no. 3 and 4 were also dependent upon deceased and were unmarried at the time of accident.

Deceased,
being the eldest earning son in the family, must have contributed towards his younger sister and brother.
Deceased being unmarried is supposed to have spent  (one half) of his income on personal expenses.
However, in this case, as the deceased was the eldest son, he is expected to contributed more in the family as he had two younger siblings.
Hence it would be fair to deduct 1/3 (one third) as personal expenses.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings MACT Case No. 49/24 (FIR no.

conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs.
Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also in another case Mangla Ram
Vs . Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
Therefore, the case does not warrant any other best evidence.
Keeping in view the facts & evidence produced by the petitioner, it is established that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle being driven by respondent No.1.
Record of medical treatment reveals that the cause of death which is consistent with the history of RTA.
. 1 is decided in favour of petitioners.
As this Tribunal has already held that R1 was responsible for the death of the deceased due to his neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Therefore, the petitioners have become entitled to be compensated for death of deceased in the above accident, but computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
Basically only three facts need to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death : (a) age of the deceased; (b) income of the deceased; and the (c) the number of dependents.
If these determinants are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
In this regard, though not quoted, reliance is placed upon, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 SCC 121.
17.
Therefore, there has to be deduction of TDS before fixing the salary of deceased for compensation.
Considering the salary of deceased, it can be fairly assumed that his salary falls under tax and he used to pay Rs. 38,000/- annually as tax from his salary.
Therefore, the income of the deceased, as on the date of the accident i.e. 18.10.223, after deducting TDS (Rs. 3,167 per month) was Rs. 69,203/- per month.
Hence it would be fair to deduct 1/3 (one third) as personal expenses.
